content.text:
The test builder now shows one step at a time, with the steps listed in the left sidebar, and every field's help panel says what happens when you leave it empty. It is pushed to [maester365/maester#2758](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2758) along with the merge from main, and the preview at http://localhost:3288/test-builder is running it.

One thing differs from what you described: a test with no `TenantType` is treated as Workforce only, not as valid in every tenant. That is what the engine and the docs both say, so the help says the same. It also says tenant type is only recorded by default; a run skips on it only when `Environment.Enforce.TenantType` is turned on.

## Layout

- **Steps in the sidebar:** nine steps, each showing a tick once visited and clean, or a red count of things to fix. The docs links sit below them.
- **One step at a time:** the tallest step is now 1,034px (Requirements) and most are under 650px, against 7,639px for the old page. Back and Next sit under the form.
- **Address keeps the step:** `/test-builder#priority` opens that step. Clicking a problem in the "things to fix" list opens the right step and puts the cursor in the field.
- **Ratings as a row:** Severity, User impact, Implementation cost and Lifecycle are a single row of choices, with only the selected option's description shown.
- **Requirements split in two:** tenant types, clouds and platforms moved to their own step, "Where it applies".
- **Phone:** the steps become a scrolling row above the form.
- **Intro text:** it moved into the first step so the other steps start at the top of the page.

## Field help

The help panels for 28 fields now explain how Maester uses the value and have an "If you leave it empty" section. Where the answer differs, the text changes between a Maester test and a custom test. Examples:

- **Tenant types:** explains Workforce (an organization's own tenant) versus External (a Microsoft Entra External ID tenant for customer or consumer accounts).
- **Licences:** an unlicensed tenant gets Skipped with `LicenseNotFound`; left empty, the test runs in every tenant and an unlicensed one gets a failure or error instead.
- **Permissions:** recorded on the result but not enforced in 3.0.
- **Platforms:** always enforced, and it means the computer running Maester, not devices in the tenant.

The text is in `website/src/components/TestBuilder/help.js`. I wrote it from the writing-tests guide and the engine's skip reasons. Please read the licence and severity wording in particular, since those describe consequences rather than quote the docs.

## Checks

- **Merge:** all 8,704 unit tests passed on the merge from main.
- **Builder:** checked in the browser at desktop and phone width, in light and dark.
- **Not run:** the full unit suite on the builder commit, since only website files changed; the file encoding, layout and builder data tests pass. The page's own script still has no automated tests.

Both changes are pushed to [maester365/maester#2758](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2758) and live in the preview at http://localhost:3288/test-builder#priority.

- **Priority icons:** each Severity, User impact and Implementation cost choice now has a small bar icon. More bars and a warmer colour mean a higher level (red for Critical, orange for High, amber for Medium, grey for Low). Info gets a blue circled "i" because it makes no risk judgement.

# Feature icons

Icons shown beside a feature's name in the report (product pages, the test list's Feature filter and a test's
Feature fact). `report/src/lib/featureIcons.ts` says which file stands for which feature.

- Source: [DanielBradley1/msicons](https://github.com/DanielBradley1/msicons) (msicons.com), commit `3d57443ed444`, taken on
  2026-11-02. Minified (whitespace and comments removed, coordinates rounded to one decimal, or to whole numbers in
  the 48-unit icons); shapes and colours unchanged.
- The icons are Microsoft's, under the same terms as `../products/README.md`: used unchanged, beside the name
  of the feature they stand for. Several are generic icons (mail, key, globe) chosen for a feature that has no icon of its own.

content.text:
Both changes are in the "Where it applies" step and pushed to [maester365/maester#2758](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2758); see them at http://localhost:3288/test-builder#environment.

- **Tenant types:** the option now reads "External (Consumer)" with Microsoft's External ID icon, and Workforce shows the Entra ID icon. The generated attribute still writes `TenantType = 'External'`.
- **External ID icon:** I downloaded it from the az-icons.com page you linked and saved it unchanged as `website/public/img/icons/external-id.svg`.
- **Clouds:** each choice has a flag:
  - United States for GCC, GCCHigh and DoD
  - China for China
  - France for Bleu
  - Germany for Delos
  - Singapore for GovSG
  - a globe for Commercial
- **Flags are drawn, not emoji:** flag emoji don't render on Windows, so these are small simplified SVGs (colours and layout, not every star).
- **Clouds help panel:** it now says which cloud is which. I wrote that line from memory (for example, that China is operated by 21Vianet and GovSG is the Singapore government cloud), so give it a read.

I checked this at desktop width in light mode only. The layout and file encoding tests passed on the tenant-type commit; nothing was run on the flags commit, and no unit tests cover the page itself.

content.content:
- Bind a parameter only when the value means the same thing to every test that binds it, and the organisation
  sets it once. A value a benchmark sets, such as a lockout threshold, is never bound: each benchmark test keeps
  its own default.
- A test never calls `Get-MtSetting` for such a value. The engine binds it, so `Get-MtTest` and the results show
  it and a `TestSettings` row can override it.
- A setting is named after what it holds, never after a test or a suite. It is registered in
  `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1` with its type, default, allowed values and, for a list of objects,
  the properties of an item; a pack names its own settings `Namespace.Key` and declares them under `Settings`
  in its `maester-pack.json`.
- The parameter's type, default and `ValidateSet` are those of the setting. The config is checked against the
  registry once before a run, so a test must not accept or default to anything else.
- Pass the value to the helpers that need it. A helper never reads a setting that tests bind, or it would ignore
  the value the test was given.
- A shim declares each bound parameter of the test it calls and passes it on. The engine binds the parameters of
  the test it runs, the shim; the function the shim calls is an ordinary call.
- A connection or transport setting that a connect command or a data helper needs, such as `GitHubOrganization`
  or `XspmExternalDataUris`, is not a test input and is read with `Get-MtSetting`. It is still registered, and
  the engine records the read on the result of the test that caused it (`SettingsRead`).

content.text:
All three requests are in and pushed to [maester365/maester#2758](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2758); the preview at http://localhost:3288/test-builder has them.

## Parameters step

- **On the step itself:** two short paragraphs say what a parameter is and what a shared setting is (one value many tests use, set once under `GlobalSettings`).
- **In the help panel:** three new sections.
  - *What a shared setting is*: why it exists, that the engine fills the parameter in, and when not to use one (a value a benchmark sets).
  - *Use a shared setting that exists*: pick it from the list.
  - *Add a new shared setting*: numbered steps that differ by mode.
    - For a Maester test: name it, register it in `MaesterSettings.psd1`, bind the parameter by hand, pass the value to helpers, document it, regenerate the builder data and run the unit tests. Two copyable snippets are included.
    - For a custom test: name it `Namespace.Key`, type it into the parameter, set it in the config, and declare it in `maester-pack.json` if it is in a pack.

The Maester-test steps use a made-up example setting, `ExcludedRegions`. The "document it" step points at the `GlobalSettings` table in the run configuration page, which is where the existing settings are listed; I didn't find a rule that requires it.

## Icons

- **Lifecycle:** Preview has a blue flask, Stable a green tick, Deprecated a grey archive box.
- **Field labels:** every field has an icon beside its label. Where the HTML report shows the same attribute (product, feature, severity, licence and so on), it is the report's icon.
- **Steps:** each step in the sidebar has an icon next to its number.
- **Mode cards:** "A test for Maester" and "My own custom test" have one each.
- **Commercial cloud:** now a coloured globe (blue with green land) instead of the outline.

These are all hand-drawn SVG, like the earlier ones, since the Nucleo connector is still not connected.

I checked the Lifecycle and "Where it applies" steps and the Parameters help panel at desktop width in light mode. I did not recheck dark mode or phone width, and no unit tests cover the page.
